KEY MESSAGE 1: A Heat Advisory is in effect for the coastal 
counties this afternoon and an Extreme Heat Watch is now in effect 
for those same counties Thursday afternoon. Additional Heat 
headlines will likely be required through the week and into the
weekend.

Heat headlines are likely into the weekend as heat index values soar 
into the 100-110 range each afternoon through mid-week and upwards 
of 115 late in the week. The daily record highs and record high 
minimum temperatures will likely be challenged at our three climate 
sites (see Climate Section for more details). Given the very mild 
overnight periods and minimal coverage of precipitation, there will 
be few instances of relief from the heat this week and into the 
weekend. 

Today: Ridging aloft will dominate over the southeastern states 
today, with high temperatures reaching into the mid 90s. With 
prevailing W to even NW flow at the surface the sea breeze will 
likely be slow to progress inland, remaining pinned at the coast 
into the early afternoon. However, dew points along the coastal 
counties are still forecast to reach into the mid 70s, yielding heat 
index values upwards of 110. A Heat Advisory is in effect for the 
coastal counties today from 11 AM to 8 PM. 

Thursday and Friday: The ridging aloft amplifies towards the end of 
the week, likely bringing the warmest temperatures of the heat wave. 
Highs on each day will likely reach into the upper 90s, with a brief 
moment of touching 100 not out of the question. Heat index values 
west of I-95 will likely reach 105-108 (Heat Advisory) with 
locations east of I-95 reaching heat index values as high as 115. An 
Extreme Heat Watch is now in effect for the coastal counties for 
Thursday afternoon.  

This Weekend: The center of ridging aloft will shift slightly 
westward, resulting in a slight downtick of temperatures. However, 
heat index values are still forecast to reach upwards of 110 along 
the coastal corridor likely necessitating additional Heat 
Advisories. 

KEY MESSAGE 2: Isolated to scattered thunderstorms will develop 
across southeast Georgia and the lower South Carolina Lowcountry, 
especially near the coast. One to two storms across extreme 
southeast Georgia may produce strong to severe wind gusts this 
afternoon. Additional thunderstorms are possible across portions of 
the region late Thursday.

Wednesday: The center of 595 DM ridge is forecast to slide west over 
the northern Gulf. As a result, NW to SE heights may align over the 
forecast area. The mid-level flow should remain a bit chaotic due to 
the deep convection upstream. Satellite water vapor indicates 
several disturbances, some on pace to ripple over the forecast area 
this afternoon. Light wnw flow may keep the sea breeze pinned to the 
coast until mid-afternoon. Following the HREF for timing and 
placement of showers and thunderstorms, the forecast will feature 
SCT to ISO PoPs. This is much greater that coverage indicated by 
recent runs of the HRRR and RRFS. Given moderate instability and 
DCAPE between 800-1000 J/kg, one or two thunderstorms between the 
Altamaha and Savannah Rivers may produce strong to severe wind 
gusts. 

Interestingly, the 0Z GFS shows an MCS tracking from the Upstate to 
the Coastal Plain this evening. Given the mid-level heights and 
lingering elevated instability, the potential for an MCS reaching 
the forecast area seems plausible. However, HREF and NAM12 indicates 
that upstream convection will dissipate before reaching the CWA. 

Thursday, H5 ridge will build west over the Deep South by the 
afternoon and evening. Near term guidance, especially the NAM12, 
indicates that a well-defined shortwave will reach the forecast area 
late Thursday afternoon into the early evening. If this feature 
arrives during the heat of the afternoon, then a solid band of 
thunderstorms may develop across the Midlands, tracking across over 
the Lowcountry. At this time, the forecast will feature a band of 
SCHC PoPs moving west to east late Thursday afternoon.
